article.title: Ubiquitous
article.description: Meaning: present, appearing, or found everywhere. Pronunciation: yoo-BIK-wi-tuhs. Example: 'Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern life.' Register: formal/academic, common in IELTS Writing Task 2 essays about technology or globalization.
article.content: Meaning: present, appearing, or found everywhere. Pronunciation: yoo-BIK-wi-tuhs. Example: 'Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern life.' Register: formal/academic, common in IELTS Writing Task 2 essays about technology or globalization.

generated.caption:
Feeling like some things are just... everywhere? There's a formal word for that!

Today's word is **Ubiquitous** (yoo-BIK-wi-tuhs)! It means present, appearing, or found everywhere. This academic word is perfect for IELTS Writing Task 2.

For example: 'Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern life.'

Save this for your next essay! Follow @TheEnglishVault for daily lessons!
generated.script: Jab koi cheez 'har jagah' ho, toh uske liye sirf 'everywhere' bolte ho? Ye word seekho! Toh the word hai Ubiquitous. Iska matlab hai jab koi cheez present ho, appearing ho, ya found ho everywhere. Matlab simply, koi cheez har jagah maujood hai. Jaise, 'Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern life.' Yaani smartphones modern life mein har jagah hain, sabke paas hain. Ye thoda formal aur academic word hai. IELTS Writing Task 2 essays mein use karne ke liye perfect hai! Toh next time jab aapko bolna ho ki koi cheez har jagah hai, har jagah dikhti hai, toh instead of 'everywhere', use karo Ubiquitous. Ab samajh aaya? slides.headlineRest: — What it means to be everywhere
slides.body: Ubiquitous (pronounced yoo-BIK-wi-tuhs) describes something that is present, appearing, or found everywhere. This formal and academic word is often encountered in IELTS Writing Task 2 essays, especially when discussing topics like technology or globalization. For example, 'Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern life,' perfectly illustrates how widespread their presence is today. It's a great word to elevate your vocabulary when describing pervasive phenomena.
